newsitem.title: UK: Options - Coffee vols firm amid choppy futures.
newsitem.headline: Options - Coffee vols firm amid choppy futures.

text.p: Coffee volatilities held steady this week as players long in robusta futures dabbled mostly in put options after another week of volatile futures markets.
But interest in cocoa options was subdued.
Traders said given the cocoa market's upside potential it would be a good time to snap up attractively-priced calls to realise profits at a later stage.
Robusta futures see-sawed from a high of $1,630 a tonne last week to a low of $1,445 this week, prompting operators to seek shelter in the options.
March volatilities rose to a high of 47 percent last week before holding at about 40-41 percent this week while May reached 44 percent before trading at 38-39 percent.
Volume was an active 4,000 lots with traders saying that the bulk of the business was outright puts buying.
"People are buying puts as a protection against the futures market," said one.
Major strikes include March $1,450 puts, May $1,500 calls, March $1,500 and $1,400 calls.
Coffee futures took a sharp upward move recently on a barrage of bullish news which triggered funds stop loss buying.
Concerns about tight Central and South American supplies and talk Vietnam could default on cheaper contracts had helped fuel the buying.
But a retracement soon set in as producers eager to cash in on high prices unloaded their nearby coffee.

All eyes will be fixed on next week's meeting in Bali, Indonesia where robusta coffee producers are expected to decide on quota allocation following a recent agreement to further cut first half 1997 robusta exports by one million bags.
In cocoa, business has been lacklustre and market makers said there was some interest to buy out-of-the money calls on May.
Implied volatilities are still relatively fairly weak at 18 percent.
"Technically the market looks as if it's getting ready for another move higher, so people are trying to buy options," said one market maker.
"We still feel the call options represent a better value buy...," he said.
About 250 call volume changed hands on Thursday.
The July calls were traded out to 20.5 percent implied volatility which traders said was still cheap for the time of the year.
Cocoa futures edged higher on Thursday on fund short-covering but it failed to clear immediate chart hurdles at 900 basis March.
The market has emerged from its contract low of 861 on March but found it difficult to make further progress on the upside, capped by origin and trade selling.
-- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
